title: $\alpha$-PFN: Fast Entropy Search via In-Context Learning
claim: Conditioning a predictive model on different information about the optimum sharpens its predictive distribution in different, complementary ways.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right plus legend column; shared baseline gray band in each
description: Three side-by-side 1-D plots show a predictive distribution over a function, titled 'Conditioning on x*', 'Conditioning on f*', and 'Conditioning on (x*, f*)'. Each panel has a gray dash-dot band for the unconditional posterior predictive and two black dots for training observations where the band pinches. A colored band overlays the gray one: green for x*, with a vertical dotted green line at the optimum location and a taller peak there. Red for f*, with a horizontal dotted red line capping the band at the optimal value. Blue for both, with a blue star at the optimum, a narrow band that peaks at the star. A legend column on the right maps the symbols, lines and colors to notation. The eye goes first to the colored bands against the gray baseline.
caption: Our base PFN estimates the Posterior Predictive Distribution (PPD) conditioned on different types of information regarding the optimum: none (unconditional case), $x^*$, $f^*$, or both. Note that this example considers a specific optimum. In practice, the optimum, and therefore the information gain, is uncertain and the ES acquisitions compute expected gain. This is typically achieved by MC sampling, where $x^*$ and/or $f^*$ samples are obtained by optimizing GP posterior sample paths. We propose to learn to predict the gain distribution directly from $D_{trn}$ using another \modelname{}.
abstract: Information-theoretic acquisition functions such as Entropy Search (ES) offer a principled exploration-exploitation framework for Bayesian optimization (BO). However, their practical implementation relies on complicated and slow approximations, i.e., a Monte Carlo estimation of the information gain. This complexity can introduce numerical errors and requires specialized, hand-crafted implementations. We propose a two-stage amortization strategy that learns to approximate entropy search-based acquisition functions using Prior-data Fitted Networks (PFNs) in a single forward pass. A first PFN is trained to be conditioned on information about the optima; second, the $Î±$-PFN is trained to predict the expected information gain by training on information gains measured with the first PFN. The $Î±$-PFN offers a flexible learned approximation, which replaces the complex heuristic approximations with a single forward pass per candidate, enabling rapid and extensible acquisition evaluation. Empirically, our approach is competitive with state-of-the-art entropy search implementations on synthetic and real-world benchmarks, while accelerating the different entropy search variants across all our experiments, with speed ups over 50x. Source code: https://github.com/automl/AlphaPFN.
